youtube.title: Why Americans Refrigerate Eggs (and Europe Thinks It's a Mistake)
youtube.description:
In most of Europe it's illegal to wash a supermarket egg. In America it's required. A US egg is scrubbed until it loses its cuticle, the natural coat that seals as many as 17,000 pores, so since 1991 US law has kept it at 45°F from the packing plant on. Britain and Europe took another path after a 1988 salmonella scare: keep the coat on the egg and vaccinate the hens. Neither egg is dirty; they're just guarded differently. The Hidden Why: the true story behind the things you use every day. #TheHiddenWhy #facts #explained
